result: Open-label 12-month s.c. IgG (0.8 g/kg/month) in 17 ME/CFS patients with recurrent infections and mild IgG/IgG-subclass deficiency: 5 of 12 per-protocol patients met the CFQ/SF-36 response criteria at month 12, 4 stopped for adverse events and 1 for worsening; LDH and sIL-2R proposed as response markers.
reason: Treatment trial that selected deficient patients; it does not measure how common IgG subclass deficiency is, so it belongs with the immunoglobulin-therapy finding

result: Open-label 12-month s.c. IgG (0.8 g/kg/month) in 17 ME/CFS patients with recurrent infections and mild IgG/IgG-subclass deficiency: 5 of 12 per-protocol patients responded (CFQ drop of at least 6 and SF-36 PF rise of at least 25) at month 12; 4 stopped for adverse events.
reason: Same intervention class (subcutaneous rather than IV immunoglobulin), adds an immunodeficiency-selected subgroup; uncontrolled and small, so weak evidence

result: Meta-analysis of 10 GET trials (n=1279): self-rated 'much/very much worse' CGI in 4% after GET vs 8% after control (RR 0.62, 0.32-1.17); treatment withdrawals 12% vs 10% (RR 1.21, NS); follow-up dropouts 11% vs 7% (RR 1.51, 1.03-2.22); GRADE certainty low.
reason: Tests worsening after GET directly and finds no excess self-rated deterioration, against the survey-based harm claim; the higher dropout rate and trial-based outcome measures limit how far it contradicts

result: Meta-analysis of 10 GET trials (n=1279): no excess self-rated deterioration (RR 0.62, 0.32-1.17) or treatment withdrawal (RR 1.21) with GET, but more follow-up dropouts (RR 1.51, 1.03-2.22).
reason: Measures safety, not the efficacy or objective-outcome claims of the PACE finding; the harms finding is the right target

result: Systematic review of 20 observational PSG/MSLT studies (1994-2021) found slow-wave sleep, apnoea-hypopnoea index, spectral activity and MSLT results inconsistent across ME/CFS studies, limited by small samples and confounding; no pooled estimates.
reason: A qualitative review of largely overlapping studies that finds inconsistency, not an independent replication; it weakly runs against a consistent objective sleep difference

result: 278 long-haulers rated current symptoms and recalled symptoms from about 21.7 weeks earlier: most symptoms (including unrefreshing sleep and PEM) fell, neurocognitive symptoms worsened, and over time they became less severe than 502 ME/CFS patients except in the orthostatic domain.
reason: Adds a symptom time course showing long COVID in general improving relative to ME/CFS; retrospective recall at one time point and no ME/CFS-criteria split, so weak

result: In 199 ME/CFS patients and 22 controls, the abnormally large fall in cerebral blood flow during head-up tilt was present in all patients regardless of %predicted peak VO2 on CPET (no, mild or more severe deconditioning).
reason: Same measure (extracranial Doppler CBF on tilt); adds that the fall is independent of aerobic fitness. Not the cited van Campen 2020 paper

result: In 199 ME/CFS patients, the tilt-induced CBF decline did not track %predicted peak VO2 categories, indicating that orthostatic intolerance is not explained by deconditioning.
reason: Extends the deconditioning-does-not-explain argument to orthostatic CBF. The cited 'van Campen 2021, Healthcare' is a different paper (2-day CPET in idiopathic fatigue), so this is not already cited

result: Exosome-associated serum mtDNA was raised in ME/CFS only after exercise, and patient exosomes stimulated significant IL-1beta release from cultured human microglia; the abstract gives no numbers.
reason: Exosomal mtDNA and microglial activation after exercise are not covered (omics-ev and muscle-exertion-ev-cargo cover EV counts and protein cargo); domain omics/exertion-EV; preprint with a thin abstract

result: Systematic review of 10 paediatric CFS/ME studies (826 patients) found recovery rates from 4.5% to 83% under 11 distinct definitions, most often based on school attendance, fatigue and physical functioning.
reason: Same outcome (recovery rate) in a paediatric subgroup; replaces the finding's unchecked adolescent-prognosis note, while showing that heterogeneous definitions prevent a pooled rate
